PUBLIC APPEARANCES BEFORE THE CITY COMMISSION:
If any person wishes to address the City Commission, the person shall sign up in the Broward Center for the Performing Arts - Mary N. Porter Riverview Ballroom lobby. A member of the City Clerk’s Office Staff will be there to assist. Speaker Cards are given to the Mayor. After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the agenda item in question, indicate support, opposition, or neutrality on the agenda item, and then proceed to succinctly state the speaker’s position or present information.
If an attorney, or any other person appears before the Commission in a representative capacity, the attorney, or other representative shall also sign up in the Broward Center for the Performing Arts - Mary N. Porter Riverview Ballroom lobby. A member of the City Clerk’s Office Staff will be there to assist. After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the client(s) being represented, and identify the agenda item in question. The speaker shall then indicate the client’s support, opposition, or neutrality on the agenda item and then proceed to succinctly state the client’s position or present information on behalf of the client(s).
Pursuant to Section 3.13 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the Mayor shall maintain order at all meetings, and the Police Department, upon instructions of the Mayor, shall expel any person from the meeting who refuses to obey the order of the Mayor in relation to preserving order at the meetings. Any person who interrupts or disturbs a City Commission meeting, or who willfully enters or remains in a City Commission meeting having been warned by the Mayor to depart and who refuses to do so, may be subject to arrest.
AUXILIARY AIDS AND SERVICES: If you desire auxiliary aids or services or both to assist in viewing or hearing the City Commission meetings or reading the agenda and minutes for the meeting, please contact the City Clerk’s Office at 954-828-5002 at a minimum of two days prior to the meeting and arrangements will be made to provide these services to you.

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\fs24 Mayor Trantalis recognized Charles King, 105 N. Victoria Park Road. Mr. King discussed his opposition to this Agenda item, citing concerns about the proposed cost increases impacting vacation rental property owners.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Porshia Garcia, Development Services Department Deputy Director. In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Ms. Garcia explained that the proposed Vacation Rental Program (Program) registration fee increases reflect full cost recovery to the City for Program management, noting that the adjustments were necessary to sustain operations due to the growing number of vacation rentals. She confirmed that the City does not profit from the Program registration fees, which cover only monitoring, enforcement, and Program administration costs.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Ms. Garcia described the varying rental rates among properties and agreed to provide additional data.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman commented that the proposed Program fee increases should not be overly burdensome and requested a comparison to neighboring municipalities. Ms. Garcia explained that Pompano Beach, Hollywood, and Lauderdale-by-the-Sea charge higher registration fees than Fort Lauderdale and that the current Program registration fee is below cost-recovery.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question, Ms. Garcia explained that Program renewal fees are lower than initial registration fees because inspections are less extensive and may be waived for homesteaded properties.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman remarked that, considering average rental revenues and regional comparisons, the proposed Program fee increases appear reasonable. Ms. Garcia confirmed that the Program fee analysis excluded duplicative costs and only reflects expenses required for operations and enforcement.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding how Program registration fees would enhance neighborhood protection, Ms. Garcia outlined measures funded by the fees, including a 24-hour hotline for neighbors, coordination with Code Inspectors and property owners, and collaboration with police to address safety concerns and illegal rentals. She explained that the Program\rquote s success depends on adequate staffing and that the increased fees would support continued responsiveness to resident complaints.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman noted a reduction in vacation rental related complaints in District 2 compared with previous years and commended staff and law enforcement for their collaborative enforcement efforts.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen introduced this Resolution which was read by title only.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\kerning2\f0\fs24 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question regarding whether funds from prior years could legally be contributed to a 401A retirement plan, Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed he is requesting the inclusion of a six point thirteen percent (6.13%) contribution to his 401A Retirement Plan and said that he would defer to staff to determine whether this payment could be applied retroactively. Mayor Trantalis recognized Jerome Post, Human Resources Department Director. Mr. Post confirmed he would need to research this aspect of Interim City Attorney Spence's request and would provide an update. Mayor Trantalis suggested separating that portion of the request from this Agenda item pending further review.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen summarized his understanding of this Agenda item: a three percent (3%) merit salary increase; retention of the adjusted salary level for one (1) year after the appointment of a permanent City Attorney; a contractual term extending through the appointment of the permanent City Attorney; and a six-point thirteen percent (6.13%) retirement contribution to his 401A, subject to confirmation. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding his term of service as Interim City Attorney and extending that timeline until the Commission appoints a City Attorney and is available to start. Interim City Attorney Spence agreed to continue serving as Interim City Attorney until the Commission appoints a new City Attorney and indicated his willingness to amend his current contract to clarify the effective term of service. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the process and what would be included in his amended contract.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s questions and concerns regarding maintaining continuity should the City Attorney selection process extend beyond October 31, 2025, Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed that he was prepared to serve through the City Attorney transition period with contractual safeguards to ensure stability until the new appointee assumes the role of City Attorney, and commented on his perspective. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s questions, Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed that he received a salary adjustment upon assuming the role of Interim City Attorney, discussed related information, including his viewpoint that maintaining that salary level during the transition period would reflect his continued workload assisting the incoming City Attorney. Interim City Attorney Spence commented on related salary ranges.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen expressed his support for a three percent (3%) merit increase and maintaining Interim City Attorney Spence\rquote s salary during the transition period. Mayor Trantalis commented on the need to determine a base salary for the City Attorney position. Commissioner Sorensen recommended that the base salary be $300,000. In response to Commissioner Sorensen's questions, Mr. Post confirmed that a $300,000 base salary would be consistent with the range for the position of City Attorney in surrounding municipalities of similar size and remarked on related information. Mr. Post explained that severance payments are normally restricted to Charter Office appointees and discussed similar scenarios. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding Interim City Attorney Spence's duration of service as Interim City Attorney and salary protections. Commissioner Sorensen expounded on his viewpoint.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst explained the context of severance pay for Commission Charter Office appointees who are contracted employees with the City, cited examples, and discussed related details. Further comment and discussion ensued. Vice Mayor Herbst remarked on resolving the 401A Retirement Plan contribution through a lump-sum payment should Interim City Attorney Spence agree to extend his employment, noting that such payment would be prospective. Vice Mayor Herbst concurred with including severance pay in Interim City Attorney Spence's Deputy Director employment contract and remarked on concerns regarding two (2) three percent (3%) merit increases. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst recommended that another attorney from the Office of the City Attorney opine on this aspect of Interim City Attorney Spence's contract.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Susan Grant, Assistant City Manager, explained that she did not request severance as part of her transition from Interim City Manager to her current role as Special Advisor to the City Manager. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding including severance pay in Interim City Attorney Spence's employment contract. Mayor Trantalis said that he is comfortable including severance in Interim City Attorney Spence's employment contract.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen introduced the Resolution as amended, which includes the following provisions for Interim City Attorney D\rquote Wayne Spence's employment contract: A three percent (3%) merit increase; a six-point thirteen percent (6.13%) Retirement Program contribution; no reduction in salary for one (1) year following his return to the position of Deputy City Attorney; and no severance pay.\kerning0\f1\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Each Commission Member disclosed verbal communications, written communications, site visits, and expert opinions received.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis opened the public hearing.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Courtney Crush, Esq., 888 East Las Olas Boulevard, Crush Law, P.A., on behalf the Applicant. Ms. Crush spoke in support of this Agenda item. In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions, Ms. Crush explained current zoning height limitations and the zoning change being sought. Mayor Trantalis noted that the height difference requested is ten feet (10') and asked whether any commercial elements would be incorporated on the ground floor. Ms. Crush explained that although the rezoning would allow mixed use, no traditional commercial uses such as retail or grocery would be included in the project. Ms. Crush said that the intent of the Applicant is to provide residential dwelling units and expounded on related information. In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding incorporating commercial entities into the project, Ms. Crush said that only building-serving amenities would be contemplated.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding explicitly restricting potential commercial uses, Interim City Attorney Spence explained the ability to record a restrictive covenant on the property to formally limit the types of permitted uses.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman requested clarification for neighbors regarding building heights. Ms. Crush noted that a fifty-five foot (55') building typically equates to five (5) stories, and a sixty-five foot (65') building equates to approximately six (6) stories, depending on floor-to-floor heights and any enhanced first-floor elevation requirements.\par
\par
Ms. Crush discussed the location of the project illustrated in a presentation slide.\par
\par
Cecelia Ward, JC Consulting President, narrated a presentation entitled \i Progresso Place Proposed Rezoning Residential.\i0\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is attached to these Meeting Minutes.\b0\i0\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized J.J. Hankerson, 905 NW 2nd Avenue, on behalf of the Progresso Village Civic Association. Mr. Hankerson discussed his viewpoint and concerns from the community related to this Agenda item. Mayor Trantalis remarked on his perspective, including previous visions for this area and its zoning, advantages and disadvantages, and remarked on the additional ten feet (10') in building height. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mr. Hankerson confirmed his past involvement regarding the vision for this area and expounded on related details and information.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman referenced Planning and Zoning (P&Z) Board Meeting Minutes related to this Agenda item that indicated both support and opposition to the rezoning. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Mr. Hankerson confirmed his understanding that any increased building heights were to be on the periphery of the neighborhood.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Bryan Perez, 842 NW 4th Avenue. Mr. Perez spoke in support of this Agenda item. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mr. Perez commented on the lack of redevelopment in this area due to its current zoning. The ability to rezone this area and add an additional ten feet (10') ensures the financial viability of redevelopment by a small developer. \par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Jonathan Nixon, 526 NE 8th Street. Mr. Nixon spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Goran Dragoslavic, Applicant, 1800 W. Broward Boulevard. Mr. Dragoslavic spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par

\par

\par

\par

\par

\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, David Bartholomew, Applicant, discussed the status of the existing structures and individuals that are affected by the project.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Tippu Sashi, 748 NW 3rd Avenue. Mr. Sashi spoke in opposition to this Agenda item. In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Mr. Sashi explained the density concerns associated with this project.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Carla Roundtree, 745 NW 4th Avenue. Ms. Roundtree discussed her opposition to this Agenda item. Mayor Trantalis noted a majority of the speakers lived in the vicinity. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Kelli Russell, 1223 Cordova Road. Ms. Russell spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Patrick Berger, 1409 SE 1st Street, Pompano Beach. Mr. Berger spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Edgar Sainz, 29835 SE 169th Street, Homestead. Mr. Sainz spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Sophia Allen, 6919 W. Broward Boulevard, Plantation. Ms. Allen spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman's question, Mr. Hankerson explained aspects of the neighborhood petitions associated with this Agenda item. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Ms. Crush explained her review of the neighborhood petitions and expounded on related information.\par
\par
Ms. Crush provided background on the genesis of the Northwest Regional Activity Center (RAC), describing the 2014-2015 discussions and planning efforts that led to the creation of zoning districts intended to promote appropriate and balanced development within the area. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s questions, Ms. Crush confirmed her understanding that several parcels in the area have remained vacant for more than twenty (20) years and elaborated on factors contributing to the lack of redevelopment. Ms. Crush agreed with Mr. Perez\rquote s earlier observation that RMM-25 zoned parcels are subject to density caps that limit the financial feasibility of redevelopment for small developers. Ms. Crush said that she is not aware of any redevelopment activity involving vacant RMM-25 parcels within Progresso Village.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman's question regarding the duration of ownership of the parcels by the Applicant, Ms. Crush explained the first parcel was obtained in 2012 and the remaining three (3) parcels were acquired within the past two (2) years.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman remarked on her perspective, comments from speakers regarding safety issues in the area, and concerns voiced by long-time area residents. She requested that redevelopment efforts involve those residents to ensure their inclusion in the process. Commissioner Glassman confirmed his understanding of ongoing efforts by the Applicant to involve the community with this project.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions regarding the affordable housing aspect of the project, Ms. Crush explained anticipation of significantly lower market rental rates and cited examples. She remarked on the Applicant's willingness to cap rents on a certain number of units that would fall within the State Statute's definition of affordable housing and expounded on related details. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Glassman noted that the topic of affordability could be discussed further when the site plan is presented to the Commission.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman's question regarding the Applicant requesting funding from the Northwest-Progresso-Flagler Heights (NWPFH) Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA), Commissioner Glassman said that there had been no request for funding from the NWPFH CRA.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman remarked on his review of the May 21, 2025, Planning & Zoning Board (P&Z Board) Meeting Minutes. In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions, Anthony Fajardo, Development Services Department Director, commented on the two (2) dissenting P&Z Board votes expressing concern for how the requested rezoning would be compatible with surrounding uses and zoning districts. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions regarding this rezoning, Mr. Fajardo confirmed it is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and Regional Activity Land Use criteria. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the process and staff's site plan review when submitted.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question about the Northwest RAC's underlying future land use designation in relation to this Agenda item, Mr. Fajardo noted the prior determination that the area required redevelopment and the land use change being the initial step. Mr. Fajardo remarked on related concerns and challenges, noting that, with Commission support, staff would conduct an ad hoc review for each rezoning request. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen remarked on input from the applicant regarding setting aside a number of units as affordable workforce housing. In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding ensuring a percentage of units as affordable housing units based upon Average Median Income (AMI) percentages, Mr. Fajardo remarked on related information, and suggested additional input from the Office of the City Attorney. Interim City Attorney Spence noted that limitations related to the affordability of the units would have to be attained through a development agreement with the Applicant. In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Ms. Crush confirmed the willingness of the Applicant to discuss that opportunity. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman explained his reasoning for supporting this Agenda item, expounded on related information, and requested that the Applicant continue to work with the neighborhood.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen reiterated his recommendation to pursue setting aside a number of affordable workforce housing units in a development agreement with the Applicant.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis explained that his vote in favor is based on supporting the zoning change only, not approval of any specific proposed site plan. He emphasized that the RAC zoning requires a higher level of design consideration, including enhanced setbacks, landscaping, and neighborhood development standards, which are not present in the current zoning for this property. He reiterated that the Commission\rquote s action tonight pertains solely to the potential and framework of what the new zoning allows, and any future site plan proposal would undergo further discussion.\par
\par
There being no one else wishing to speak on this item, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman made a motion to close the public hearing and was seconded by Commissioner Glassman. Roll call showed AYES: Vice Mayor Herbst, Commissioner Glassman, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman, Commissioner Sorensen, and Mayor Trantalis.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst introduced this Ordinance on the First Reading which was read by title only.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24 Commissioner Glassman emphasized the significance of this Agenda item and explained his reasoning for pulling it for further discussion. He discussed feedback from District 2 condominium residents who received notices from First Responders stating that radio signal issues hamper communication within these buildings. Commissioner Glassman expounded on his perspective that it is the City's responsibility to ensure adequate radio signal communications, reiterated feedback from condominium residents related to First Responders recommending outside vendor solutions. He remarked on the significant remediation costs and the need for further education for condominium owners and management. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
City Manager Williams shared that when this matter came to the attention of the City's leadership team, multiple departments took steps to address the issue, which included developing an outreach and educational plan. She expounded on efforts to expedite reissuing the Request for Proposals (RFP).\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Chris Cooper, Assistant City Manager. Mr. Cooper confirmed the accuracy of Commissioner Glassman's concerns related to the State Statute requiring that buildings of a certain size, structure and type maintain adequate two-way radio communication, cited examples of possible solutions, and discussed related information. Further comment and discussion ensued. Mr. Cooper commented on staff referring building management to licensed and accredited vendors with the ability to address this issue.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman discussed his related conversations with Florida House of Representative Chip LaMarca and the need to address this issue at the State level. Mr. Cooper concurred and discussed staff efforts. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
City Manager Williams remarked on updated Fire-Rescue Department communications to buildings that address State Statute requirements and building notices.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Glenn Marcos, Procurement Services Department Director. Mr. Marcos explained the reasons for rejecting all the RFP proposals and staff efforts to reissue a new RFP.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mr. Marcos confirmed there will be a future solicitation for constructing a new cellular tower to address communications issues.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Jason Swift, Information Technology Services Division Manager. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mr. Swift explained information regarding the need for constructing a new cellular tower. Part of the new RFP includes ensuring that respondents determine a total communications coverage solution. Commissioner Glassman stressed the importance of that solution and reiterated this communication issue is the responsibility of the City.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Mr. Swift confirmed that materials used in building construction impacts communications and cited examples. Mayor Trantalis remarked on the responsibilities of building developers to ensure building materials permit radio communications and discussed his perspective. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
Commissioner Glassman noted that buildings that have had no communication issues in the past now have issues, cited an example of a building and its resiliency efforts, and expounded on related information. He reiterated his viewpoint that this issue is the responsibility of the City. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\cf1\f1\par
\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Jason Miller, Fire-Rescue Department Fire Marshal. Fire Marshal Miller noted recent conversations with Commissioner Glassman and explained that Fire-Rescue personnel are following current code requirements. He pointed out that LEED requirements for "green" certified buildings can create issues with public safety radio signals inside those buildings. State law mandates that the City enforce minimum standards for radio signal strength. If Fire-Rescue personnel encounter inadequate radio coverage during an inspection or emergency call, they must cite the building for a code violation, irrespective of whether it was constructed correctly. Fire Marshal Miller confirmed improvements to building notices have been implemented, which includes options available to address radio signal interference in order to comply with current Code. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Mr. Swift explained efforts to improve communication signals in the City, noted the need for additional communication towers in the City, explained associated information, and cited examples. Mr. Swift discussed limitations posed by building construction and cited an example. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen concurred with Commissioner Glassman's viewpoint and confirmed the importance of addressing this issue. Commissioner Sorensen noted this issue also occurs in City schools, discussed his understanding of the communication issue that causes weak to non-existent signal transmission, and expounded on safety concerns. Commissioner Sorensen noted discussions to address this concern in schools with the School Board of Broward County (School Board) Superintendent and explained their efforts to analyze communication needs and provide funding.\par
\f1\par
\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Police Department Chief William Schultz. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question about an interim solution, Chief Schultz explained that using the cellular portion of Police Department personnel radios in schools can strengthen the communication signal. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Chief Schultz explained details associated with addressing indoor and outdoor signal transmission and cited examples. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the causes of inadequate signal transmission.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen remarked on the need to identify buildings that lack good signal strength. Chief Schultz confirmed and discussed related efforts. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Mr. Marcos anticipates reissuing the RFP by the end of the year. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\f1\par
Commissioner Glassman made a motion to approve this Agenda item and was seconded by Commissioner Sorensen.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis recognized Chris Cooper, Assistant City Manager. In response to Commissioner Sorensen's questions, Mr. Cooper explained his discussions with Commissioner Sorensen regarding his recommended Ordinance amendments. \par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen's first proposed amendment is to reduce the time period for applicants denied by the Board of Adjustment from two (2) years to one (1) year. This would allow applicants to reapply sooner if they present new information or factors that were not previously considered. Interim City Attorney D'Wayne Spence indicated they had no objection to this change and it would be incorporated before the Second Reading.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen's second proposed amendment is to eliminate Section B(vi) on page six (6) of the Ordinance, Mr. Cooper explained that this permits staff to approve de minimis variance requests. However, if a directly affected neighbor objects in writing, the request would be escalated to the Board of Adjustment for a formal review.\par
\par
\cf1\f1 Mayor Trantalis passed the gavel to Vice Mayor Herbst at 10:47 p.m.\cf0\f0\par
\par
Interim City Attorney Spence explained that variance requests are quasi-judicial matters requiring a hearing to determine whether criteria are met. He noted that while administrative variances streamline minor cases, objectors are entitled to due process, which can be accommodated through a hearing before a zoning administrator or by forwarding the matter to the Board of Adjustment, the appropriate body for such determinations. Other municipalities, including Plantation, employ similar procedures for administrative variance appeals. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed that section could not be removed and reiterated that the first proposed amendment would be made between the first and the second readings.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Herbst's question, Interim City Attorney confirmed the need for this Agenda item to be introduced.\par
\par
\cf1\f1 Commissioner Sorensen introduced this Ordinance on the First Reading which was read by title only.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Trantalis provided an overview of this Agenda item, remarked on previous discussions at the October 7, 2025, Commission Meeting regarding this topic, and discussed resident communications to Commission Members indicating overwhelming neighborhood support for streetlights in Melrose Park.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, City Manager Williams explained backup information includes an update and details of the October 14, 2025, meeting with Melrose Park residents, which staff and Commissioner Beasley-Pittman attended. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding the recommended number of streetlights discussed at the Melrose Park HOA Meeting on October 14, 2025, Commissioner Glassman quoted an email from the Melrose Park HOA President suggesting an alternative proposal for one hundred fifty (150) streetlights at intersections and bus stops and remarked on additional language in that email. City Manager Williams commented that number could have been an arbitrary number versus staff's recommended proposal for five hundred fifty-five (555) streetlights.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman commented on her viewpoint regarding the alternative recommendation for the reduced number of streetlights, which was not defined. She discussed the initiative taken by Melrose Park residents to pursue streetlights in their neighborhood, which resulted in four hundred (400) signatures that were gathered in seven (7) days and in support of streetlights. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis commented on concerns regarding the monthly cost for streetlights that seems excessive and recommended staff renegotiate with Florida Power and Light (FPL). Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis inquired about individuals who had signed up to speak and had previously provided their comments. In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Interim City Attorney Spence noted that speakers who had not previously shared their perspectives would still be given the opportunity to speak.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question about the costs for five hundred fifty-five (555) Melrose Park streetlight units, Gladys Reyes, FPL, explained the expenses are related to an agreement with the City (Agreement). The Agreement is part of FPL's lighting tariff for new outdoor streetlight installations, specifically for streets and parking lots applicable to new installations that utilize LED fixtures for both public and private customers. \par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Ms. Reyes explained details of upfront costs and the monthly charges. Mayor Trantalis noted his understanding that the monthly cost amortizes the capital expenses, maintenance, and energy costs for the streetlights. In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions, Ms. Reyes explained the Agreement is for ten (10) years and auto renews after five (5) years, and is approved by the Florida Public Service Commission. The energy cost per month is approximately seven hundred eighty-eight dollars ($788) for five hundred fifty-five (555) streetlight units.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman remarked on additional aspects included in an email from the Melrose Park HOA President regarding post lights on individual properties and remarked on his understanding regarding additional lights on private property. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Ms. Reyes explained residents requesting additional lights on their property would be in their monthly bill. Any lighting requests on City rights-of-way need to be requested by the City.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Duke Davis, 363 E. Dayton Circle. Mr. Davis spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
\cf0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Christopher Persaud, 550 E. Campus Circle. Mr. Persaud spoke in opposition to this Agenda item.\par

\par

\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Reginald Youngblood, 3841 Jackson Boulevard. Mr. Youngblood spoke in support of this Agenda item.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Novelette Porter, 485 W. Evanston Circle. Ms. Porter spoke in opposition to this Agenda item commenting on an opportunity for a lower cost. Mayor Trantalis remarked on the procurement aspect of this Agenda item. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Christopher Paul, 545 E. Campus Circle, New Hope Seventh Day Adventist Church and School Pastor. Pastor Paul commented on the possible impact of streetlights on Melrose Park properties and the neighborhood, including gentrification. Mayor Trantalis commented on the consistent millage rate and the impact on homesteaded properties in Melrose Park. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman remarked on her perspective and discussed meeting with Pastor Paul.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman noted that significant progress had been made with the Melrose Park HOA, expressed concern regarding FPL's monthly cost, and said that he would have liked to hear from the individual who had proposed a solar-powered alternative. Commissioner Glassman confirmed support of starting with one hundred fifty (150) streetlights, \kerning2 which is a reasonable incremental approach, rather than immediately installing all five hundred fifty-five (555) streetlights\kerning0 originally proposed and would allow the Melrose Park neighborhood to evaluate the results and decide whether additional lighting should be added. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman emphasized that, as the District 3 Commissioner, she had thoroughly vetted the initial five hundred fifty-five (555) streetlight unit proposal with residents during multiple community meetings. Melrose Park residents clearly expressed their preference for the original plan. She opposed reducing the scope, noting that there were no measurable criteria to support the lower number. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman confirmed her full support for moving forward with the project as initially proposed.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mayor Trantalis explained his understanding of the monthly costs that included energy and the lease payment for the streetlights and streetlight poles.\par
\par

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Commissioner Glassman reaffirmed his support for public safety and expressed ongoing concerns regarding requirements for Bi-Directional Amplifiers (BDAs) in buildings, which are essential to facilitate communications between police, fire personnel, and other first responders (First Responders). He noted continued feedback from condominium buildings in District 2 and discussed a recent email from a property in Hendricks Isles that he shared with Fire-Rescue Department Chief Stephen Gollan and City Manager Rickelle Williams. \par
\par
Commissioner Glassman requested that staff provide an explanation of how they plan to address this issue. He discussed the financial burden that installing BDAs would impose on condominium owners, who are already facing multiple financial challenges and cited examples. Commissioner Glassman explained his viewpoint that the responsibility for ensuring effective First Responder communication systems and related technology should lie with the City. He noted discussions with Chip LaMarca, Florida House of Representatives Member, who indicated that other coastal cities experiencing similar growth and development are not encountering the same two-way radio signal problems. Commissioner Glassman reiterated the need for further clarification from staff, and expounded on related information.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis remarked on earlier discussions on this topic and related responsibilities. Commissioner Glassman remarked on various related scenarios brought to his attention, cited examples, and expounded on his perspective. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Chris Cooper, Assistant City Manager. Mr. Cooper said that the State, through the Florida Fire Prevention Code, places this financial burden on the property owners of certain properties and explained related information. Commissioner Glassman discussed additional information and details provided by condominium residents and remarked on possible less expensive alternatives. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding radio signal evaluation. \par
\par
City Manager Williams expounded on staff efforts to address this issue from numerous perspectives, cited examples, and confirmed that the Commission would be kept updated.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding increasing the number of portable radio tower trailers, \cf0 Ron McKenzie, Information Technology Services Department Director, explained portable radio towers would not penetrate through buildings and are used only in cases of emergency. \par
\par
\cf1 In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mr. McKenzie said that the Request for Proposal for a new public safety communications radio tower is anticipated to be opened by the beginning of 2026.\cf0\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst said this issue relates to enforcement of the State's Building Code. In response to Vice Mayor Herbst's question regarding whether excess funds in the Building Permit Fund could be utilized to offset costs to buildings experiencing this issue, City Manager Williams confirmed this option is being reviewed by Development Services Department staff. Vice Mayor Herbst noted that buildings in District 1 also experience similar two-way radio communication issues and suggested staff take a proactive approach and research his recommendation and expounded on his viewpoint. Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed his office would research and update the Commission. Commissioner Glassman confirmed his support of Vice Mayor Herbst's recommendation.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman discussed the need to analyze all buildings City-wide to determine two-way radio communication deficiencies.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Fire-Rescue Chief Gollan. Chief Gollan explained annual inspections for commercial buildings are done to make related determinations in addition to \kerning2 real-time reports of two-way radio communication issues during any type of First Responder call \kerning0 and explained related information.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' remarks regarding The Adderley, Chief Gollan confirmed that BDAs were installed in that building during construction and were activated prior to receiving its Certificate of Occupancy (CO).\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman requested a report regarding buildings in District 3 with two-way radio communication deficiencies. Chief Gollan confirmed, explained that deficiencies are determined during annual testing for two-way radio deficiencies, and said that approximately nineteen percent (19%) of buildings in the City have been cited.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen reiterated similar concerns discussed at today's Conference Meeting related to this issue in schools and efforts to address this need with the School Board of Broward County (School Board). He expounded on his viewpoint and requested staff to include schools in its report of buildings with radio deficiencies.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, City Manager Williams confirmed a list of buildings with two-way radio deficiencies exists and continues to be updated.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman made a motion to approve this Agenda item and was seconded by Commissioner Beasley-Pittman.\v\par
}

A member of the City Clerk’s Office Staff will be there to assist. Speaker Cards are given to the Mayor. After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the agenda item in question, indicate support, opposition, or neutrality on the agenda item, and then proceed to succinctly state the speaker’s position or present information.
If an attorney, or any other person appears before the Commission in a representative capacity, the attorney, or other representative shall also sign up in the Broward Center for the Performing Arts - Mary N. Porter Riverview Ballroom lobby. A member of the City Clerk’s Office Staff will be there to assist. After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the client(s) being represented, and identify the agenda item in question. The speaker shall then indicate the client’s support, opposition, or neutrality on the agenda item and then proceed to succinctly state the client’s position or present information on behalf of the client(s).
Pursuant to Section 3.13 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the Mayor shall maintain order at all meetings, and the Police Department, upon instructions of the Mayor, shall expel any person from the meeting who refuses to obey the order of the Mayor in relation to preserving order at the meetings. Any person who interrupts or disturbs a City Commission meeting, or who willfully enters or remains in a City Commission meeting having been warned by the Mayor to depart and who refuses to do so, may be subject to arrest.
AUXILIARY AIDS AND SERVICES: If you desire auxiliary aids or services or both to assist in viewing or hearing the City Commission meetings or reading the agenda and minutes for the meeting, please contact the City Clerk’s Office at 954-828-5002 at a minimum of two days prior to the meeting and arrangements will be made to provide these services to you.

minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\fs24 Commissioner Beasley-Pittman congratulated Shari McCartney on her appointment but expressed concerns about the proposed $350,000 employment contract, noting that this amount exceeds the salary listed in the job announcement and represents a significant increase over previous City Attorney contracts. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman commented that this proposed salary could set an unfavorable precedent and requested further discussion.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis explained that his salary negotiations aimed to align with the City Manager's salary and expounded on related information. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the City Attorney's role as a Charter Officer, the position's significant responsibilities, limited job security, and the goal of attracting and retaining top talent.\par
\par
Jerome Post, Human Resources Department Director, stated that the salary range in the recruitment brochure was based on regional comparisons and was reviewed by the City Attorney Search Committee (CASC).\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst expressed support for Ms. McCartney as the City Attorney but opposes the proposed salary. He cited examples and commented on the need for consistency with posted salary ranges.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding an appropriate salary level, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman responded that the salary should reflect the candidate's experience and responsibilities but should not be equated with the City Manager's position. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman discussed her viewpoint that the City Manager's position entails broader oversight and management of a larger workforce and requested clarification of previous City Attorney salaries. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis expounded on his perspective regarding the appropriateness of his salary negotiations with Ms. McCartney and remarked on related details. Commissioner Glassman concurred.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst suggested a salary approximately ten percent (10%) above the Deputy City Attorney's salary, which would equate to approximately $320,000. He discussed his viewpoint and concerns regarding surpassing the posted salary ranges, standard Human Resources Department practices for salary compensation and hiring within established ranges.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Mr. Post explained that the salary range in the recruitment brochure was developed using regional comparisons, which were in the high $200,000 range and reviewed by the CASC. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Sorensen discussed his perspective and support for Ms. McCartney's negotiated salary, noted the demanding nature of the City Attorney position and related information. In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Mr. Post confirmed that all Charter Officers serve at the Commission's discretion and can be terminated without cause, subject to contractual severance provisions.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman remarked on his support of Ms. McCartney's negotiated salary, noting it is appropriate relative to the Office of the City Attorney salary ranges, and cited examples. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman question regarding prior policy, Vice Mayor Herbst discussed his recollection, noted differences, cited examples, and expounded on his viewpoint. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman reiterated her opposition, elaborated on her perspective, and clarified that her concerns were unrelated to Ms. McCartney's qualifications.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen introduced this Resolution which was read by title only.\par
}

Las Olas Boulevard, on behalf of ECOAR, LLC (Applicant/Developer) of the parcel located at 1000 SW 26th Street. \kerning2 In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions regarding traffic concerns, Ms. Knapik discussed her observations of traffic along streets adjacent to the property as illustrated in a presentation entitled \i\f0 EDGEWOOD OAKS - APPLICATION FOR REZONING\i0\f1 . Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
\b\i\f0 A copy of the presentation has been attached to these Meeting Minutes.\b0\i0\f1\par
\kerning0\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions, Ms. Knapik discussed details of the development's planned traffic ingress and egress, noting it would not impact St. Jerome Church. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the related traffic study and planned traffic calming measures.\par
\par
\kerning2 Commissioner Sorensen discussed community feedback regarding concerns related to traffic, stormwater, and tree preservation. Traffic issues include maintaining SW 26th Street as a one-way roadway and addressing southbound residential neighborhood cut-through traffic on SW 12th Terrace and SW 13th Avenue. Ms. Knapik confirmed the Applicant's commitment to installing traffic calming road tables and agreement to retain all stormwater on-site to prevent runoff onto adjacent properties. She explained tree preservation efforts, which include working with staff and Broward County permitting authorities. The Applicant has committed to placing more than one (1) acre of the site under a tree conservation easement to preserve mature trees in perpetuity. The Applicant will relocate existing healthy trees into the parcel's conservation areas and will plant new street trees to enhance the tree canopy.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions regarding tree preservation, Ms. Knapik said there would be a net gain of trees per Broward County regulations that require replacement at a ratio greater than one-to-one for trees that cannot be relocated. She reiterated that twenty percent (20%) of the site will be placed under a conservation easement, preserving mature tree canopy in perpetuity. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Sorensen reiterated his understanding.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Ms. Knapik discussed planned improvements, which include efforts with City engineering staff. In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Ms. Knapik confirmed that trees inside the fence will be preserved in a twenty-five foot (25') City easement.\par
\par
In response Commissioner Sorensen's question about neighborhood concerns related to onsite parking in townhouse development, Ms. Knapik said that each townhouse will provide two (2) to three (3) on-site parking spaces, exceeding minimum code requirements, along with additional guest parking to avoid overflow parking on adjacent residential streets. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding the development's capacity to absorb stormwater from the adjacent neighborhood, Ms. Knapik clarified that the proposed development's stormwater system is intended to manage runoff from the site, not from surrounding neighborhoods. She noted that the City has existing drainage infrastructure within the adjacent swale.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen discussed the property's conservation easement to preserve the existing tree canopy. Ms. Knapik confirmed and elaborated on additional conservation plans. Further comment and discussion ensued.\kerning0\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman pointed out that this discussion highlights broader planning considerations and referenced earlier feedback from the Planning and Zoning Board that suggested a higher level of review/coordination in the future and expounded on his viewpoint. \par
\par
\cf1\f0 There being no one else wishing to speak on this item, Commissioner Sorensen made a motion to close the public hearing and was seconded by Commissioner Glassman. Roll call showed AYES: Commissioner Beasley-Pittman, Commissioner Sorensen, Vice Mayor Herbst, Commissioner Glassman, and Mayor Trantalis.\par
\par

\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding guidance on this Agenda item, Mayor Trantalis\cf0\kerning2\f1 emphasized the importance of delivering a City Hall building that reflects Fort Lauderdale\rquote s identity, ambition, and long-term vision that is reflected in the FTL City Hall Partners proposal. Mayor Trantalis expounded on his perspective and confirmed his confidence that the FTL City Hall Partners premium cost could be addressed through reducing overall square footage, refining programming needs, and applying value engineering while maintaining the integrity of the design.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis said that his number one (1) ranked proposal is FTL City Hall Partners and his number two (2) ranked proposal is Balfour Beatty.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman commented on his viewpoint that all four (4) teams were highly qualified. He pointed out that the two (2) primary distinguishing factors are the Internal Rate of Return (IRR)/bid amount and indirect construction costs and noted that these are the two (2) metrics which teams can be held accountable. Commissioner Glassman said that the Commission\rquote s role at this stage is to select the right long-term partner, highlighted the importance of experience, and expounded on his perspective.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst explained that he could not support the current procurement strategy, recommended rejecting all proposals, and issuing a new solicitation. Vice Mayor Herbst noted his consistent advocation for a bifurcated City Hall with a ceremonial City Hall in downtown and staff operations that do not interact with the public at an existing property on Cypress Creek Road.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst discussed his secondary preference to construct a new City Hall adjacent to the new Police Department Headquarters, which would create a consolidated government campus. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis remarked on past and future opportunities for public engagement on this topic and noted the Infrastructure Task Force Advisory Committee's recommendation for a P3 approach. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman confirmed the need for Strategic Communications to ensure the public is consistently informed and engaged in this process going forward.\cf1\kerning0\f0\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen introduced this Resolution to proceed with the unsolicited proposal submitted by FTL City Hall Partners as the first ranked proposal, Balfour Beatty as the second ranked proposal, Fort Lauderdale Civic Partners as the third ranked proposal, and FTL Beacon collaborative as the fourth ranked proposal which was read by title only.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\kerning2\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis provided background information and noted that the purpose of this Agenda item is to receive the presentations from the four (4) shortlisted proposers for a new City Hall (Project). He acknowledged the efforts of the Infrastructure Task Force Advisory Committee and the extensive community engagement that took place, which included multiple outreach events aimed at reimagining City Hall, and noted that feedback received from those events was compiled and presented to the Commission.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized City Manager Rickelle Williams, who acknowledged the staff members who contributed to this effort. City Manager Williams discussed the progress regarding the unsolicited proposal path for the Project and provided additional details and information.\par
\par
Assistant City Manager Ben Rogers provided an overview of the City\rquote s evaluation process of the four (4) shortlisted proposals and details of the independent evaluations by external consultants, Jacobs Project Management Co. (Jacobs), and PFM Asset Management, LLC (PFM). \par
\par
Mr. Rogers noted that supplemental proposal information packages were issued in response to Commission feedback. Those additional materials were incorporated into the staff\rquote s recommendation report. Mr. Rogers outlined the presentation process, beginning with presentations from the City\rquote s consultants, followed by a litigation overview from Interim City Attorney D'Wayne Spence and presentations from the four (4) shortlisted proposers. Following all four (4) presentations, staff will provide additional analysis, including the City\rquote s financial capacity and available resources, followed by public comment and Commission discussion. Mr. Rogers clarified that, pursuant to statute, the Commission would be asked to rank all four (4) proposers, including a primary and an alternate.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Jonathan Jordan, Jacobs Project Executive. Mr. Jordan narrated a presentation entitled \i City of Fort Lauderdale City Hall: Review of Supplemental Information.\i0\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda item.\par
\b0\par
\i0 In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding like-for-like comparisons, Mr. Jordan said that differences in the design complexity of the four (4) proposals directly affects overall Project costs, cited examples, and noted that cost variations are primarily driven by the scope of each proposal. The interior space square footage and programming are a like-to-like comparison. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Sergio Masvidal, PFM Financial Advisors, LLC, Managing Director. Mr. Masvidal narrated a presentation entitled \i City Hall Proposal - Capital Stack and Plan for Finance.\par
\par
\b A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda item.\par
\b0\par
\i0 In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding the reason that this report did not more strongly recommend alternative financing approaches like those used for the water treatment plant, Mr. Masvidal explained that the report was intentionally structured to reflect the evaluation criteria and assumptions established for the solicitation to ensure consistency and fairness. Commissioner Glassman remarked on his perspective and commented on the City's strong financing record.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding City financing, Mr. Masvidal explained that three (3) of the four (4) proposers indicated they would work with the City should it wish to finance the Project directly. Fort Lauderdale Civic Partners was the exception and less flexible regarding alternative financing approaches. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, City Manager Williams recommended that the City participate in Project financing and suggested ten percent (10%) equity in the project. Commissioner Sorensen agreed.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Interim City Attorney Spence. Interim City Attorney Spence explained that Exhibit 2A contains a litigation review of the four (4) proposals and explained related information. Staff summarized their disclosures and supplemented them with independent docket searches and are included in the exhibit for each proposer.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding the four (4) proposers having pending litigation matters with any contractors or subcontractors, Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed, reiterated that those disclosures are listed in each proposer\rquote s backup information, and recommended that the Commission inquire directly with each proposer during the presentations. \par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' questions regarding the City being a party to any of those litigation matters, Interim City Attorney Spence discussed two (2) cases. City litigation involving Fire Station 54 and PGAL, the Architect of Record with FTL Beacon Collaborative, which was recently settled. Interim City Attorney Spence also noted litigation involving the exterior lighting on the Las Olas Garage involving Arquitectonica, Lead Architect with FTL Beacon Collaborative.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions related to litigation and safety disclosures with some of the proposers, Interim City Attorney Spence advised that these issues are not disqualifying, per se, but are factors for the Commission to consider when evaluating and ranking the proposals. Interim City Attorney Spence reiterated that related concerns could be further explored during proposer presentations, and explained information associated with the proposer\rquote s certified litigation disclosures. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions regarding potential risk issues identified in Exhibit 1 and whether those issues should affect proposer evaluations and rankings, Interim City Attorney Spence explained that the Commission should decide whether those issues constitute a disqualifying factor and that the Commission could seek further clarification during each presentation. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman noted a scrivener\rquote s error in Exhibit 1, page 13 of 27, where PGAL was incorrectly listed as the Architect of Record for the FTL Beacon Collaborative Team. Interim City Attorney Spence confirmed and clarified that PGAL is the architect of record for the FTL City Hall Partners Team.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question, Interim City Attorney Spence provided an update on the City\rquote s litigation involving Arquitectonica for the lighting and mesh on the Las Olas Garage , stating that the matter is ongoing and currently in the discovery and deposition phase.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Mark Jennings, Balfour Beatty Vice President of Finance (BB Team). Mr. Jennings along with Kobi Karp, Kobi Karp Architecture and Interior Design, John Pearch, Balfour Beatty Vice President of Operations; Todd Orr, DLR Group Principal, Peter Moore, Chen Associates President and Chief Executive Officer, and Don White, Johnson Controls narrated portions of their presentation.\par
\par
Mr. Karp introduced the BB Team design video.\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is part of the back to this Agenda item. \par
\par
A copy of the video is available through the Office of the City Clerk.\i0\par
\par
\b0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question regarding how the BB Team would ensure local job generation and local employment on the project, Mr. Pearch explained their approach, which begins with community townhalls, discussed outreach through its trade partners to encourage hiring local workers for construction activities.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question about a specific percentage commitment to hiring local, Mr. Pearch said that direct employment by the prime contractor is limited because much of the workforce is outsourced through subcontractors. Mr. Pearch remarked on prior related efforts that they would be willing to do for this project.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question regarding whether the four-point twenty-four percent (4.24%) bond interest rate assumption was realistic for debt, Mr. Jennings said this rate reflected pricing at the time of proposal submission in early November 2025, is considered realistic, and expounded on related information.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question regarding the wide variations of the proposals related to indirect soft costs, overhead/administrative costs, and the contingency amount, Mr. Jennings explained their proposal attributes lower costs to operational efficiencies, extended pre-Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) design and subcontractor awards, and risk transfer to the developer. Mr. Jennings said that a one point five to two percent (1.5% - 2%) construction contingency for the GMP is reasonable and responsible.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen\rquote s question regarding the BB Team\rquote s sustainability measures, Mr. Jennings stated that no specific sustainability thresholds or LEED certification level were priced into the proposal, noted their extensive experience with LEED projects, and confirmed they are willing to explore those options. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen\rquote s question regarding BB Team\rquote s low square footage price, Mr. Jennings explained that their pricing advantage is driven by a fundamentally simple, cost-efficient design approach focused functionality and efficiency and remarked on related information. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding the BB Team having any design or professional negligence or Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) violations with municipal projects, Mr. Jennings said there are none to his knowledge. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's question regarding a longer interim agreement period and whether there is an advantage to moving more quickly to a comprehensive agreement, Mr. Jennings said a longer interim agreement reduces pricing risk and contingency costs by allowing greater design maturity before the GMP is determined. A shorter interim agreement may accelerate timing but typically results in higher contingency and greater cost uncertainty. Mr. Pearch expounded on related risk details.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question about the term availability payment (AP), Mr. Jennings explained that the City would not make APs during the design and construction phases. The APs begin after the facility is completed and handed over to the City for use. The APs are fixed annual amounts that the City will pay over a period of thirty (30) years and include use, operations, and maintenance. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding what occurs at the end of the thirty (30) year concession period, Mr. Jennings explained that the agreement would include specific residual life standards for major building components and cited examples. When the concession period ends, ownership, operations, and maintenance fully revert to the City, and the City assumes responsibility going forward.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recessed the meeting at 2:18 p.m.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis reconvened the meeting at 2:25 p.m.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Chris Hodgkins, Meridiam Developer & Equity Member, Fort Lauderdale Civic Partners (FLCP) Team. Mr. Hodgkins discussed the FLCP Team's proposal and narrated the first portion of their presentation and a related video was shown.\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is part of the back to this Agenda item. \par
\par
A copy of the video is available from the Office of the City Clerk.\par
\par
\b0\i0 The following FLCP Team members narrated their respective portion of the presentation: Mackenzie Welsh, Meridiam Developer & Equity Member; Bernard Zyscovich, Zyscovich Architecture; Nick Philips, Meridiam Developer & Equity Member; Jeffrey Gouveia, Suffolk Construction; Sheryl Dickey, Dickey Consulting; and Dodie Keith, Keith Engineering. \par
\par
Ms. Dickey explained the FLCP Team's commitment to local hiring and workforce inclusion as part of the Project delivery and operations.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman's question regarding percentages associated with local hiring, Mr. Hodgkins confirmed and explained the use of local demographics, zip code-based hiring, inclusive leadership practices, and union partnerships. He discussed similar results from prior public partnerships. Mr. Hodgkins confirmed related documentation from the \i Construction and Craft Worker's Local Union No.\'b71652 of The Laborers International Union of North America\i0 submitted to City Clerk David Soloman.\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the documentation is attached to these Meeting Minutes.\par
\b0\i0\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding the thirteen-point five percent (13.5%) post-tax internal rate of return (IRR), Mr. Philips explained that IRR is not guaranteed. It is a conservative, upper-range planning assumption used in the absence of a finalized contract. The actual return is expected to be negotiated downward as Project risks, responsibilities, and terms are clarified through a Comprehensive Agreement.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding FLCP's escalating AP, Mr. Philips explained that both fixed and escalating AP structures are commonly used and that the FLCP Team is amenable to either approach. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Sorensen's questions regarding delivery structure, financing, sustainability standards, and Project timeline, Mr. Philips confirmed that FLCP Team is open to Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Maintain (DBFOM) delivery, but not Design, Build, Finance (DBF), emphasizing the importance of long-term operational alignment. The FLCP Team is open to flexible structured financing, including City-funded debt, but developer equity participation and long-term O&M responsibility are non-negotiable success factors. Sustainability costs already include net-zero capability and prioritizes WELL Certification, the global standard from the International WELL Building Institute (IWBI) that certifies buildings and spaces are designed and operated to improve the health and well-being of occupants, over Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED). Mr. Philips noted that the assumed seven (7) month interim agreement period reflects a conservative timeline and explained related information.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen remarked on his understanding of risk and compliance issues associated with a municipal project. In response to Commissioner Sorensen\rquote s questions regarding concerns related to design or professional negligence, OSHA violations, or similar issues, Mr. Philips said that from the development side, there is none he is aware of.\f1\par
}

\cf0 Commissioner Glassman corrected for the record comments from speakers regarding this Agenda item.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman sought legal clarity on whether and under what circumstances the City can modify improvements under the ILA without triggering legal conflict, specifically related to the \ldblquote consent not unreasonably withheld\rdblquote provision. City Attorney Shari McCartney explained that a key factor in determining whether consent is being \ldblquote unreasonably withheld\rdblquote would be whether a proposed change would burden the project. She noted that the BMCDD would have the opportunity to object, and the City could respond by asserting that such an objection is unreasonable if it does not materially burden the project. Further comment and discussion ensued. Commissioner Glassman discussed his recollection of working with Bahia Mar developers to scale back the project, discussed information regarding the amenity package for the Park, and expounded on his perspective.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, City Manager Williams said Park improvements are limited to $1,000,000 under the ILA and there are separate Parks Bond funds available for other improvements. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the accurate amount of funding from the BMCDD. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Herbst commented on his understanding and requested a written commitment with specific funding information from Bahia Mar developers and the BMCDD regarding their financial commitment for Park amenities. \par
\par
Mayor Trantalis remarked on his understanding that numerous aspects of this issue will be clarified, including financial contributions for the Park and replacing basketball courts with pickleball courts east of the Coastal Construction Control Line (CCCL) that involves significant permitting risks. He commented on the basketball courts remaining at their current location. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding a deadline, City Manager Williams explained that the ILA includes a January 2027 deadline for all Park improvements and discussed information included in backup materials. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
City Manager Williams explained that clear Commission direction regarding the number of pickleball courts is required before staff can meaningfully evaluate permitting feasibility and move the project forward.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, City Manager Williams explained that staff has only conducted preliminary outreach to the State and cannot confirm feasibility of constructing pickleball courts east of the CCCL at this time. City Manager Williams commented on the ability to construct pickleball courts on the existing basketball court footprint. \par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Herbst's question, Mayor Trantalis remarked on possible issues related to nonconforming use. Ben Rogers, Assistant City Manager, explained that there are varying levels of permitting and noted that the complexity of permitting depends on the scope of improvements. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Sorensen stated his view that the basketball courts should remain in their current location. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman discussed her viewpoint that the basketball courts should remain in their current location if it does not violate the ILA. \par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Herbst's question, City Attorney McCartney explained her interpretation of the ILA provision related to not unreasonably withholding consent. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis expressed interest in pursuing a collaborative compromise that meets both developer and community recreational goals. Commissioner Sorensen agreed and recommended establishing a single point of contact to engage with the BMCDD, suggesting that the Mayor, in coordination with the City Attorney, lead discussions to explore potential options and report back to the Commission. \par
\par
Commissioner Glassman reiterated concerns about meeting timelines required under the existing ILA and expounded on his viewpoint regarding meeting the needs of the entire City. Mayor Trantalis stated that he would meet with the BMCDD, together with the City Manager and City Attorney, to work toward a solution. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\cf1\par
Commissioner Glassman made a motion to defer this Agenda item and was seconded by Vice Mayor Herbst.\par
}
