\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized William Brown, Budget Advisory Board (BAB) Chair. Chair Brown provided an overview of BAB\rquote s efforts on the Fiscal Year 2027 (FY 2027) Budget and Commission priorities. Chair Brown narrated a presentation entitled \i Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Review Fund\i0 .\par
\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda item.\b0\i0\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's questions concerning the BAB\rquote s recommendation to maintain the current millage rate, which passed by a five (5) to two (2) vote, and clarification regarding the two dissenting positions, Chair Brown explained that the dissenting BAB members favored opposite approaches. One member supported lowering the millage rate, while the others advocated for increasing the millage rate. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s questions regarding the proposed $444 Fire Assessment Fee (Fee), City Manager Williams confirmed it would be for full cost recovery and noted that a portion would be used to fund the Holiday Park Fire Station. Vice Mayor Herbst noted that Emergency Medical Service (EMS) costs should not be included in the Fee. Further comment and discussion ensued. Chair Brown said that the BAB supports full cost recovery and remarked that it is a more transparent approach. Vice Mayor Herbst emphasized the need to ensure that the Fee includes only legally permissible costs benefiting real property and would exclude EMS and other non-qualifying expenses. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Laura Reece, Office of Management and Budget Director. Ms. Reece explained that Stantec Consulting completed a full cost allocation analysis for the previous year and was subsequently updated. The methodology identifies allowable operating and capital costs and provides for recovering capital costs associated with new fire stations over a three (3) year period. \par
\par
Commissioner Herbst questioned the reasonableness of recovering the cost of a fire station over three (3) years when the facility has a forty (40) year useful life. Ms. Reece said that the three (3) year cost recovery period reflects the City\rquote s decision to cash fund fire station construction rather than financing it. Commissioner Herbst questioned the methodology and discussed other financing structures. In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s question, City Auditor Reilly said he had not reviewed Stantec's Fee study. Commissioner Herbst requested that City Auditor Reilly review the Fee study. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman recommended discussing a potential millage rate increase as part of an evaluation of how the City balances taxes, fees, and assessments and their collective impact on residents.\par
\par
Chair Brown acknowledged the need to balance the impact of a millage rate increase on taxpayers with the City\rquote s financial needs, noted that consideration should also be given to potential property tax reform, and discussed other considerations. Chair Brown said that the City is at a financial turning point, with expenses growing faster than revenues, remarked on competing considerations and suggested that smaller, incremental millage rate increases could avoid the need for larger increases in the future. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, City Manager Williams confirmed that the Fee study would be provided to City Auditor Reilly and that any necessary follow-up would occur by July 2, 2026. Commissioner Herbst requested that the review be completed as expeditiously as possible. Vice Mayor Sorensen said that the information should be provided to the entire Commission.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman requested Commission discussion regarding increasing the millage rate. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding the deadline to set the millage rate. \par
\par
Commissioner Herbst remarked on his support of a millage rate decrease and said that he would accept maintaining the current rate, but opposes an increase, particularly considering the proposed property tax reform referendum. In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question, Commissioner Herbst advocated for at least a point one (0.1) millage rate reduction that would provide modest property tax relief to residents and confirmed the ability to identify corresponding City budget reductions.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s questions regarding the impact of a point one (0.1) millage rate reduction, Ms. Reece confirmed an approximate $7,000,000 revenue reduction.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman confirmed his opposition to reducing the millage rate, support of maintaining the current 4.1193 millage rate with a focus on budget efficiencies rather than reducing revenues, and expounded on his viewpoint.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen said that he supported maintaining the current millage rate and was open to considering a decrease. He requested that City Manager Williams provide additional analysis at the July 2, 2026, Commission Meeting regarding the potential impact of a point one (0.1) millage rate reduction. \par
\par
In response to City Manager Williams' question regarding whether the Commission would like to consider an analysis of alternative millage rate reductions and corresponding budget reductions, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman confirmed, noted the position of other Commission Members, and requested staff also provide an analysis of a point one (0.1) millage rate increase. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to City Auditor Reilly\rquote s question, Commissioner Herbst requested that he evaluates the methodology used in the Fee study and provide his opinion, with particular attention to the recovery of capital costs for a new fire facility over a three (3) year period. Commissioner Herbst expounded on his viewpoint that requiring current taxpayers to pay the full cost of a facility within three (3) years may be inequitable when the facility has a significantly longer useful life that will benefit future taxpayers. Commissioner Herbst said that whether the City cash funds or finances a new fire station facility should not determine how its costs are allocated over its useful life and remarked on the applicability of generally accepted accounting principles and financing costs.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Oliver Cale, BAB Member. Mr. Cale discussed his recommendation for comprehensive cost reductions and operational efficiencies before determining the millage rate. Mr. Cale recommended evaluating the City\rquote s structural budget challenges, projected ad valorem revenue losses, and costs for a new City Hall to develop a sustainable long-term approach. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, City Manager Williams said BAB\rquote s feedback was consistent with discussions the BAB has had over the past several months. City Manager Williams acknowledged opportunities for additional strategic budget reductions and intends to present those to the Commission before bringing forward the proposed FY 2027 Budget.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst discussed his advocacy for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its productivity gains. Vice Mayor Sorensen concurred. In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, City Manager Williams discussed efforts to implement AI as a staff tool. Commissioner Herbst recommended allowing staff to identify innovative uses of AI.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman raised concerns with cyber security and privacy protections associated with AI. In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s questions regarding those concerns, Commissioner Herbst explained aspects of Microsoft Copilot that operates within the City\rquote s Microsoft 365 platform and provides a more controlled environment for organizational data.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Ron McKenzie, Information Technology Services Department Director. Mr. McKenzie discussed the purpose and importance of implementing AI tools in a secure manner with safeguards to ensure users cannot access unauthorized information. Mr. McKenzie confirmed that AI applications can improve employee efficiency, effectiveness, and enhance services to residents and businesses. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst expounded on his use of AI and ways staff could utilize. Mr. McKenzie noted the importance of verifying AI information and remarked on related details. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Chair Brown discussed a report sent to the Commission over the weekend, stating that the BAB had reached a consensus not to release it due to discrepancies. BAB will provide a revised report at its upcoming August meeting to ensure the Commission receives accurate and complete information.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recessed the meeting at 1:27 p.m.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen reconvened the meeting at 2:12 p.m.\par
\par
City Manager Williams provided an overview of the FY 2027 preliminary budget, stating it takes a conservative, forward-looking approach, significantly reducing departmental requests while maintaining key investments in public safety, infrastructure, capital projects, and technology. Staff recommends FY 2027 serve as a transition year to increase efficiency and prepare for potentially tighter financial conditions in FY 2028.\par
\par
Laura Reece, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director, and Parth Patel, OMB Assistant Budget Manager, narrated a presentation entitled \i FISCAL YEAR 2027 PRELIMINARY BUDGET GENERAL FUND.\par
\par
\b A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda item.\b0\i0\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen remarked on his support of Fiscal Year 2027 funding allocation for sustainability and waterway initiatives such as marine vessels, Living Seawall permit fee waivers, and a waterway trash skimmer initiative. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Ms. Reece discussed a strategy to use existing Pension Obligation Bond Fund reserves and modify the timing of contributions that would reduce City contributions by approximately $2,100,000 annually over the bonds\rquote remaining six (6) years without impacting pensions. In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s question, Ms. Reece confirmed that this strategy would be distributed over the remaining life of the Pension Obligation Bonds. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding additional strategies to reduce General Fund expenditures without impacting services to residents or employees. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst's question regarding whether staff had considered extending the current fleet replacement cycles, Ms. Reece said staff would research. Further comment and discussion ensued. Vice Mayor Sorensen concurred with the cost saving recommendations. City Manager Williams recommended directing those funds toward infrastructure, capital projects, and other future Commission priorities rather than recurring expenditures.\par
\par
City Manager Williams noted Mayor Trantalis\rquote request for a Commission discussion on public outreach related to potential property tax reform to provide staff with direction regarding future public outreach efforts. Vice Mayor Sorensen concurred. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
City Attorney McCartney explained that staff communications to residents related to property tax reform may only include information educating the public and should not advocate for or against a particular position. In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, City Attorney McCartney reiterated that Commission Members may provide information to educate the public regarding property tax reform but should refrain from advocating for or against a particular position. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Kevin Pulido, Office of Strategic Communications (Stratcom) Director. Mr. Pulido narrated a presentation entitled \i Property Tax Reform and City Impacts.\par
\par
\b A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda item.\b0\par
\par
\i0 City Manager Williams said that staff would begin public outreach on property tax reform and requested Commission feedback regarding the outreach efforts as soon as possible so staff can make modifications.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Chair Brown requested clarification and guidance on how BAB works with Stratcom and remarked on the option and benefit of related webinars. Vice Mayor Sorensen remarked that this would be a topic at his District 4 Pre-Agenda Meeting. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman requested comprehensive educational materials to help address residents\rquote questions about property tax reform. City Attorney McCartney confirmed that BAB Members are subject to the same restrictions as staff and Commission Members and cannot advocate for or against potential property tax reform. City Manager Williams confirmed that Stratcom could develop multi-level public information packages. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst sought clarification regarding the distinction between advocacy and an elected official expressing his opinion regarding property tax reform. He noted his understanding that State law permits elected officials to express their personal views for or against an issue. City Attorney McCartney confirmed that elected officials may express personal opinions but should distinguish their personal views from advocacy in their official capacity. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question regarding whether the public education campaign could identify potential budget reductions and service impacts should property tax reform be approved by voters, City Manager Williams recommended having a comprehensive discussion to identify potential budget reductions before including that information in the materials. Further comment and discussion ensued. \par
\par
Commissioner Glassman remarked on questions from District 2 residents and expounded on his support of identifying potential reductions in advance of the November 2026 election to provide residents with a transparent understanding of the impact that property tax reform could have. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
City Manager Williams said staff will present the Commission with potential budget reductions and preliminary concepts related to property tax reform and the City Hall project on July 2, 2026.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Paul Renneisen, 3111 NE 56th Avenue. Mr. Renneisen requested specific information regarding potential employee furloughs and service impacts should property tax reform be approved.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Douglas Meade, 2612 NE 21st Terrace. Mr. Meade commented on public outreach related to potential property tax reform and discussed his recommendations. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Barbie Pearson. Ms. Pearson confirmed her support of additional public education regarding property tax reform, including a taxpayer impact statement, newsletter, and an informational forum presenting multiple perspectives before the November 2026 election.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen recognized Ray Jordan, 2341 NW 15th Court, on behalf of the Dillard Park Homeowners Association. Mr. Jordan requested additional public education explaining how property tax reform could affect funding for services and projects addressing community needs in District 3. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Trantalis said that he had been contacted by attorney Gene Pettis who informed him that City Manager Williams wished to end her employment with the City and subsequently received the terms for ending her employment, which the City Attorney incorporated into a Mutual Separation Agreement and First Amendment to the City Manager's Employment Agreement.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman recommended considering the Walk-on item at the end of the meeting to allow the City Manager to conduct the scheduled City business. Further comment and discussion ensued. There was a consensus to consider the item immediately.\par
\par
City Manager Williams thanked the Commission, staff, and community for the opportunity to serve and reflected positively on her tenure with the City.\par
\par
City Attorney McCartney summarized the material terms of the proposed Mutual Separation Agreement (MSA). City Manager Williams would immediately relinquish her duties, receiving sixty (60) days' paid notice, followed by unpaid administrative leave through December 1, 2026, to assist with the transition as needed, and twenty (20) weeks of severance pay plus accrued leave and other eligible benefits.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, City Manager Williams confirmed that she was satisfied with the proposed terms of the MSA. In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding clarification of the provision allowing the City Manager to perform compensated work during the unpaid leave period, asking whether such work would require Commission approval or could be authorized by the Interim or subsequent City Manager, City Attorney McCartney explained that the provision contemplated City Manager Williams being available to assist with the transition or other matters as needed and said that the Acting City Manager, not the Commission, would make that determination. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman remarked on her positive view of City Manager Williams' leadership and accomplishments and thanked her for her service.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Vanessa Apotheker, 712 SW 9th Terrace, Tarpon River Civic Association President, and Council of Fort Lauderdale Civic Associations (CFLCA) District 4 Representative. Ms. Apotheker expressed appreciation for City Manager Williams' leadership and conveyed the communities' positive feedback and support.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Beverly Chambers, 431 NW 17th Avenue. Ms. Chambers commented on her support for City Manager Williams.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Barbie Pearson, 2420 SE 17th Street. Ms. Pearson expressed appreciation for City Manager Williams' leadership and dedication.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Tina DeMarco, 1329 NE 7th Avenue. Ms. DeMarco urged City Manager Williams to reconsider leaving the City, citing strong community support for her leadership and professionalism.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Amanda Wilson, 900 SW 12th Street. Ms. Wilson acknowledged City Manager Williams' community and affordable housing efforts and raised concerns about recurring City Manager turnover.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis clarified that City Manager Williams' separation would take effect on Friday, July 3, 2026, and that appointment of an Interim or Acting City Manager would be addressed tonight.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen remarked on City Manager Williams' leadership and accomplishments, acknowledged that the Commission had not adequately supported her, and characterized her departure as a significant loss.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman noted that City Manager Williams was not being terminated, thanked her for her service, and his support of the MSA. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst expressed appreciation for City Manager Williams' service and collaboration.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst introduced this Resolution which was read by title only.\par
}

\par

{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Williams provided a historical overview of the Agenda item and reiterated her recommendation to reject all bids due to solicitation irregularities and differing interpretations of the City's requirements. Mayor Trantalis reviewed his understanding of the procurement process and circumstances leading to this appeal. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, City Attorney McCartney explained the status of the appeal and the matter before the Commission. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Mark J. Stempler, Esq., on behalf of Motorola. Mr. Stempler spoke in support of denying the appeal and discussed Motorola's legal position.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding whether the appeal constituted a de novo hearing, City Attorney McCartney explained that the appeal was not required to proceed as a de novo hearing. She noted that the Commission could decide the matter based on the existing record and its discretion to receive additional testimony.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, City Attorney McCartney clarified that although the Commission could receive additional testimony, its review should remain limited to the matters raised in the written appeal and should not include new or unrelated issues.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Pratima Raju, on behalf of Communications International, Inc. (CI). Ms. Raju spoke in opposition to the Chief Procurement Officer's denial of CI's bid protest and narrated a presentation entitled\i Communications International Appeal of Procurement Decision.\par
\i0\par
\b\i A copy of the presentation is attached to the Meeting Minutes.\b0\i0\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Danielle Sanabria, on behalf of Communications International, Inc. Ms. Sanabria continued the presentation and spoke in opposition to the Chief Procurement Officer's denial of CI's bid protest.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, City Attorney McCartney explained that the Commission's role was to review the Chief Procurement Officer's denial of the bid protest. She emphasized that the Commission's review was limited to the specific issues raised in the original protest and could not be expanded on appeal to consider additional alleged deficiencies in Motorola's proposal. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, City Manager Williams reiterated her recommendation to reject all bids due to solicitation irregularities and differing interpretations of the procurement requirements.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman recalled that the Commission had previously decided to hear the appeal rather than reject all bids and restart the procurement process, in part due to testimony from Fort Lauderdale Professional Firefighters Local 765 President Keith Costa regarding the urgency of moving forward with the public safety radio system, and the life-safety implications of a further delay. He noted that restarting the procurement could delay the project by several months.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman discussed the positions presented by CI and Motorola and requested clarification regarding the proper scope of the appeal. City Attorney McCartney reiterated that the Commission should consider only the issues and information contained within CI's original bid protest.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst's question, City Attorney McCartney disputed that there had been an issue with the timeliness of staff's production of information.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst's question regarding whether CI had requested information that was not provided until after its protest had been denied, Ms. Sanabria confirmed that certain requested information was received after the denial, said that negotiations had not yet occurred when the protest was filed, and maintained that CI's position throughout the protest was that Motorola had submitted a noncompliant proposal. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst's question, City Attorney McCartney confirmed staff's position was that it had not knowingly advanced a proposal that failed to comply with the mandatory requirements of the solicitation, and said that the Chief Procurement Officer had determined Motorola's proposal met those requirements. \par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen noted his understanding that the issue before the Commission was whether the Chief Procurement Officer acted within his authority and complied with applicable law and procedure. City Attorney McCartney confirmed. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen's questions regarding discussions reflected in staff transcripts presented by CI, City Attorney McCartney explained that those discussions occurred during negotiations. Glenn Marcos, Procurement Services Department Director, confirmed that the discussions occurred following the notice of intent to award to Motorola and maintained that issues arising during subsequent negotiations were outside the scope of CI's protest and should not be considered as part of the appeal. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding proposal rankings, Mr. Marcos explained that pricing represented thirty percent (30%) of the overall evaluation. Mr. Marcos said that CI ranked first in four (4) of five (5) categories before pricing was factored into the evaluation and confirmed that Motorola ranked first overall once pricing was included.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' additional questions, Yvette Matthews, Assistant City Manager, explained that the City had prepared a presentation comparing Motorola's proposal with the Request for Proposal (RFP) requirements. Ms. Matthews noted that the City's technical consultant reviewed Motorola's proposal and determined that, although ambiguities in the RFP resulted in differing interpretations of certain technical specifications, Motorola's proposal aligned with the RFP requirements. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen's questions, Mr. Marcos reviewed the competitive procurement process and said that during subsequent negotiations following the notice of intent to award, staff had greater discretion to clarify proposal responses and negotiate with the highest-ranked proposer to obtain the best value. Further comment and discussion ensued regarding negotiation transcripts.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Joe Carpenter, on behalf of CI. Mr. Carpenter spoke in support of the appeal.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding how rejecting all bids and restarting the procurement process would benefit CI, Mr. Carpenter explained that a new solicitation could clarify specifications that had been subject to differing interpretations and allow the proposers to compete under the same requirements. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Ellyn Bogdanoff, on behalf of Motorola. Ms. Bogdanoff spoke in support of denying the appeal and maintained that Motorola had complied with the mandatory requirements of the RFP. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question regarding whether CI had ranked first in four (4) of five (5) evaluation categories and whether pricing ultimately changed the ranking, Mr. Marcos stated that he would need to review the evaluation results to confirm. Mr. Marcos said that the Evaluation Committee recommended Motorola and that city public safety officials ranked Motorola first. Commissioner Glassman emphasized the importance of considering those recommendations and expounded on his viewpoint.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst expressed support for rejecting all bids and restarting the procurement process, citing concerns related to the process and potential litigation. He maintained that a clear solicitation could be completed within approximately three (3) months and would place the City in a more secure legal position. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst made a motion to reject all bids and restart the procurement process. The motion died for lack of a second.\par
\par
Commissioner Beasley-Pittman and Mayor Trantalis questioned the benefit of restarting the procurement process and explained their perspectives. Commissioner Herbst said that restarting the procurement process would provide an opportunity to clarify ambiguous requirements and reduce the likelihood of another procurement dispute. Commissioner Glassman opposed restarting the procurement process, noting that the Commission had previously considered and rejected that approach and emphasized the importance of consistency. Commissioner Herbst said that the Commission's prior decision had been made without the benefit of the full presentation, the discussion currently taking place, and maintained that the additional information could have affected that decision. Commissioner Glassman disagreed, noting that he had previously met with both parties and reviewed the relevant information. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman made a motion affirming the Chief Procurement Officer's denial of the protest and was seconded by Vice Mayor Sorensen.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Mayor Trantalis recognized Brad Kaine, Public Works Department Director. Mr. Kaine reviewed information related to Agenda Items R-7 and R-8, as detailed in the Agenda item backup.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question regarding the timing of the City's decision to participate with the Solid Waste Authority (SWA), Mr. Kaine explained that the Commission was considering two (2) related actions, approval of the Facilities Amendment and approval of the Second Amendment. Mr. Kaine recommended that approval of the Facilities Amendment be conditioned upon unanimous approval of the Second Amendment by all participating municipalities. Vice Mayor Sorensen discussed his perspective as the Commission's SWA representative. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst supported conditional approval of this Agenda item as a means of preserving the City's participation while providing additional time to negotiate provisions more favorable to the City, including guaranteed representation on the Executive Committee, provided the Second Amendment containing the opt-out provision is approved. Mayor Trantalis concurred.\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen clarified that, if the Second Amendment is approved, the City could opt out following the RFP process for any reason within the specified one (1) year period. He noted that an opt-out decision would not need to be based solely on price and could include other considerations, such as the City's inability to secure permanent representation on the Executive Committee.\par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized City of Sunrise Mayor Michael J. Ryan. Mayor Ryan spoke in support of the Agenda item and discussed the roles of Broward County and Broward County municipalities participating in the SWA. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis' question, Mayor Ryan clarified that the Executive Committee does not have independent decision-making authority and serves in a recommending capacity, with final decision-making authority resting with the SWA Governing Board. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Herbst's question, Mayor Ryan supported the concept of conditional approval as a means of demonstrating the City's intent to participate while preserving safeguards associated with approval of the Second Amendment. Mayor Ryan expressed confidence that the Second Amendment would receive unanimous approval from the participating municipalities.\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman's question, Mayor Ryan provided an update regarding Broward County municipalities supporting participation in the SWA. Commissioner Beasley-Pittman confirmed her support. Further comment and discussion ensued.\par
\par
Commissioner Herbst introduced this Resolution as amended that the Facilities Amendment be conditioned upon unanimous approval of the Second Amendment by all participating Broward County municipalities which was read by title only.\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis recognized Acting City Manager Christopher Cooper. Acting City Manager Cooper introduced Director of the Office of Management and Budget Laura Reece.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Ms. Reece narrated the presentation and provided a summary of changes since the last joint meeting in June 2026.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\b\i\f0 A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda\b0\i0 \b\i item.\b0\i0\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question regarding the timing of growth, Ms. Reece explained the tax roll for 2026 reflects any growth that happened in the year before January 1, 2026.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Budget Advisory Board Chair William Brown. Chair Brown narrated a presentation focused on the future designed to assist the Commission in setting priorities in January 2027.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\b\i\f0 A copy of the presentation is part of the backup to this Agenda\b0\i0 \b\i item.\b0\i0\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 The Budget Advisory Board endorsed the FY 2027 budget as presented by staff by unanimous vote at their last meeting. Chair Brown said the proposed budget is realistic, responsible, meets all current needs, and is balanced as required for FY 2027 with priorities for public safety.\par
The Board identified five key areas for concentrated effort in the FY 2028 budget process. Concerns included housing affordability; the millage rate; business taxes, fees, and permits; a slowdown in the development market due to high construction costs and interest rates; and property tax reform.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question regarding a Flagler Village development project, Chair Brown agreed the project would add significantly to the tax rules during the year in which it gets its Certificate of Occupancy (CO).\par
\par
In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question regarding service reductions, Chair Brown suggested possibly reducing park programs, special events and parades, and other things that have a big impact on city services and cost. \par
\par
Chair Brown said it is important that people understand the impact to services if property tax reform happens. Once guidance is received from the Commission\rquote s Prioritization Workshop, cost reductions can be scrutinized in greater detail.\par
\par
Commissioner Glassman commended the Budget Advisory Board for their work and commitment and confirmed that they endorse the proposed budget. Chair Brown recognized the tremendous contribution of the staff of the Office of Management and Budget.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s inquiry about staff collaboration, Chair Brown said they work well together and he has no suggestions for improvement.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question regarding possible immediate cost savings, Chair Brown suggested not-for-profits and CRA. In the future, everything should be considered, excluding key elements like public safety, water, sewer, stormwater, and the infrastructure needs required for life safety and sustainability.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s request for additional detail on the sources of the savings identified, Ms. Reece explained the $10.9 million in strategic reductions incorporated in the proposed budget. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Ms. Reece explained that these reductions prepare the City for FY 2028, before any potential property tax reform. If an additional $17 million reduction in revenues is realized in FY 2028, additional strategies will have to be implemented in collaboration with all operating departments. A structural balanced budget means ongoing revenues are tied to ongoing expenses. Capital costs are one-time costs and can be considered for reduction as well.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s concerns regarding cutting the grant writing budget, Acting City Manager Cooper said the cut was based on historical spending, and many grants do not require outside assistance. Staff will continue to aggressively pursue grant opportunities. If additional assistance is needed staff can return to the Commission. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Herbst stated that increasing efficiency is imperative when revenue drops. Continuing to deliver on the expectations of constituents while having less revenue coming in should be the focus rather than cutting services.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Budget Advisory Board member Olivier Cale. Mr. Cale said he was not able to vote on the budget and would not have voted to approve because more structural reform should be considered. He expressed concerns about the cost of the City Hall project and said affordability should be at the center of the budget process and finding ways to offer relief to citizens.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s request, Mr. Cale said the City Manager\rquote s Office, Office of Strategic Communications, and the Office of the Police Chief have grown significantly in the past years.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2160\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s and Mr. Cale\rquote s comments, Chair Brown said department heads have been more efficient than they have in a long time in this government. He referenced an exercise undertaken by the previous City Manager asking each department what measures they\rquote d take if they had to cut their budgets by 5%. Commissioner Herbst requested to see the results of that exercise.\cf1\f2\par
}

minutes_note:
{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fswiss\fprq2\fcharset0 Arial;}{\f1\froman\fprq2\fcharset0 Times New Roman;}}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis opened the public hearing.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Miles D. Jolley, 101 NE 3rd Avenue, Suite 1910, designated representative of the applicant, Sharon Duncan. Mr. Jolley gave an overview of the history of the request and appeal and spoke in favor of setting a de novo hearing. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question, Mr. Jolley said this is only for the rear setback variance on the shed which was denied by the Board of Adjustment (BOA). \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Mr. Jolley said the unique hardship shown was that the applicant was unaware that the contractor used was unlicensed and that the criteria and facts were the same for all three variances requested. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question regarding title insurance, Mr. Jolley explained that the applicant owned the property for approximately 10 years before undertaking these improvements. The contractor obtained permits for the main structure but not for the accessory unit. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Each Commission Member disclosed verbal communications, written communications, site visits, and expert opinions received. \f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Vice Mayor Sorensen provided additional background based on his visit to the site and conversations with both the owner and the President of River Oaks Civic Association. He added that the contractor was investigated due to lack of licensure and was found guilty. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Mr. Jolley explained that the mechanical setback and the minimum lot size variances were approved by the BOA based on the criteria given but the rear setback was not approved.\par
\par
\pard Mayor Trantalis recognized D'Wayne Spence, Deputy City Attorney. Mr. Spence provided an overview of the case.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question regarding new state statutes for accessory dwelling units, Mr. Spence said units must still meet local zoning and setback requirements. \par
\par
In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Mr. Spence explained that the structure in question meets the definition of a habitable dwelling unit based on its square footage even though it does not have kitchen or bathroom facilities and is not considered a shed because it is larger than allowed by city ordinance.\par
\par
Mr. Spence said the Commission is tasked with determining whether the case record provides evidence that the BOA based their decision on lawful criteria. He read the definition of hardship according to city code and the five criterion the BOA must consider. \par
\par
Mayor Trantalis recognized Ted Inserra, President of River Oaks Civic Association, 901 SW 19th Street. Mr. Inserra said the Association and neighbors unanimously support Ms. Duncan and believe the proper person has been punished, the contractor.\par
\par
In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question, Vice Mayor Sorensen said Ms. Duncan was unaware that the contractor was not licensed for the totality of the work for which he was hired. \par
\par
There being no one further wishing to speak on this item, Vice Mayor Sorensen made a motion to close the public hearing, seconded by Commissioner Glassman. Roll call showed: AYES: Commissioner Glassman, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman, Vice Mayor Sorensen, and Mayor Trantalis; NOT PRESENT: Commissioner Herbst\par
\par
Vice Mayor Sorensen stated his view that the evidence is applicable to two of the variances and should be applicable to the third and therefore the evidence used by the BOA is not competent and a de novo hearing is needed. \par
\par
\pard\nowidctlpar Vice Mayor Sorensen introduced this Resolution setting a de novo hearing to consider the appeal before the City Commission at 6:00 p.m. on October 6, 2026, which was read by title only.\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f0\par
}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis recognized Ian Cohen, 1250 S. Pine Island Road, Plantation, CEO of Inspected. Mr. Cohen said he worked with the state in creating the new legislation and believes the proposed fee schedule regarding private providers is not in compliance with the statute.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mr. Cohen\rquote s comments, Mr. Fajardo said the previous methodology can no longer be used, which resulted in some fees increasing and some decreasing due to changes made to meet the statute\rquote s July 1, 2026 deadline. He added that all building fees will need to be changed again in January 2027 and greater parity with the statute will be seen at that time.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question regarding caps, Mr. Fajardo said it may be possible to offer a deeper discount, but he is not sure what options are available at this time. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mr. Fajardo introduced Juan Rodriguez, Development Services Department Assistant Director. Mr. Rodriguez said private provider fees used to depend on the specific case, but the old methodology can no longer be used. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Mr. Fajardo said the fees have never fully covered department costs and will continue not to be covered 100% due to the legislation. He said a consultant was hired to create a fee schedule which will comply with the statute and more changes will be brought to the Commission in December. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Mr. Fajardo confirmed that fee revenue goes to the building fund, not the general fund. Assistant City Manager Yvette Matthews stated the current building fund balance is approximately $26 million, and the operating budget is $30 million.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote concerns, City Attorney McCartney said the fees must be carefully calculated, and it would be premature to institute a cap now. Acting City Manager Cooper added that modeling will need to be done using the new statutory requirements. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Acting City Manager Cooper explained that private provider fees are meant to cover the administrative cost of managing the program and, although those fees will now be less because of the new statute, everything should level out once the full fee schedule is complete. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote and Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s concerns regarding providing relief for private providers in the short term, Acting City Manager Cooper suggested deferring the ordinance.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\f0 Vice Mayor Sorensen made a motion to defer Second Reading of this Ordinance to September 15, 2026, seconded by Commissioner Glassman\cf1\f2 .\par
}

{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fswiss\fprq2\fcharset0 Arial;}{\f1\froman\fprq2\fcharset0 Times New Roman;}{\f2\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}

\viewkind4\uc1\pard\nowidctlpar\f0\fs24 Mayor Trantalis opened the public hearing.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Aaron Gonzalez, 2149 NE 56th Place. Mr. Gonzalez expressed support for Fire-Rescue and adequate funding for public safety but opposition to the cumulative impact on residents. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Laura Reece, Office of Management & Budget (OMB) Director. In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s request, Ms. Reece addressed additional facilities, wage and benefit increases, and increases in vehicle expenses and pointed out that approximately $12 million in budget reductions were realized. She added that the increase per family over last year is approximately $15 per month which includes the millage rate, voter approved debt, stormwater assessment, and fire assessment. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s question, Ms. Reece outlined the various efficiencies and revenue enhancements which comprised the $12 million in budget reductions. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 There being no one further wishing to speak on this item, Vice Mayor Sorensen made a motion to close the public hearing and was seconded by Commissioner Glassman. Roll call showed: AYES: Commissioner Herbst, Commissioner Glassman, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman, Vice Mayor Sorensen, and Mayor Trantalis\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Stephen Gollan, Fire-Rescue Department Chief. In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s request, Chief Gollan explained that per state statute, the fire assessment fee may only be utilized to recover costs relating to Fire, not to Rescue and ambulance costs. He stated that the fee may increase during certain years when a new station or equipment comes online, and then decrease during other years. The City\rquote s fees fall right in the middle amongst all municipalities with fire departments in Broward County and he believes this shows efficiencies do exist. He stressed that the department strives to ensure overtime costs are kept as low as possible and said building inspection and transport revenues contribute 73% of the annual cost of Fire-Rescue. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question regarding fees charged to condominium and apartment owners, Chief Gollan reiterated that fees are assessed per residential unit and are based on Florida statute. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Chief Gollan said it is true that the department undertakes an annual exercise to identify possible efficiencies before the fire assessment fee is calculated.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Ms. Reece confirmed that the overall picture regarding taxes and fees is taken into consideration by the Budget Advisory Board, staff, and the Commission. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Discussion continued with Chief Gollan regarding the number of service calls received, how many staff are needed per vehicle, the difference between efficiency and economy, total personnel numbers this year compared to last, and comparisons with municipalities of similar size. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis and Acting City Manager Cooper read their respective portions of the BGT-7 budget script.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\b\i\f0 A copy of the budget script is attached to these Meeting Minutes.\b0\i0\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Glassman introduced this Resolution, which was read by title only.\cf1\f2\par
}

\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Aida Nesimi, 1010 Seminole Drive. Ms. Nesimi stated her opinion that the City\rquote s current budget and decision-making do not correctly anticipate the future of Fort Lauderdale for the next 4-10 years and said more needs to be done to attract jobs and young people to the area.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Vice Mayor Sorensen provided information on public-private partnerships for infrastructure which are currently happening and expressed his opposition to the Live Local Act.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Glassman stated he has noticed an increase in the number of young people and questioned the data showing a decrease.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Beasley-Pittman invited young people to voice their opinions to the Commission.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Amy Moore, 1475 Cypress Creek Road. Ms. Moore thanked the City Manager and Commission for their support for the Early Learning Coalition and the school readiness program.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Aaron Gonzalez, 2149 NE 56th Place. Mr. Gonzalez asked the Commission to distinguish needs from wants, immediate obligations from items that can be phased, and core services from discretionary spending before adopting the budget.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Ted Inserra, President of River Oaks Civic Association, 901 SW 19th Street. Mr. Inserra said people need a break from all the increases. He stated that Commission members should not be urging people not to vote for Amendment 3.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Glassman clarified that he has never told people how to vote but has urged people to be educated. Vice Mayor Sorensen added that the City does not take a position on this and is barred from telling people how to vote. Mayor Trantalis stated he has pointed out the pros and the cons of the impact of what voting for Amendment 3 will do but has never taken a position one way or the other. Commissioner Herbst confirmed with the City Attorney that the City can provide education but cannot take a position, however an individual Commissioner can advocate any way they like.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2430\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 There being no one further wishing to speak on this item, Vice Mayor Sorensen made a motion to close the public hearing and was seconded by Commissioner Glassman. Roll call showed: AYES: Commissioner Herbst, Commissioner Glassman, Commissioner Beasley-Pittman, Vice Mayor Sorensen, and Mayor Trantalis\par

\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question, Ms. Hayes said two of her properties front on Third Avenue but the parking is only accessible from the alley.\par

\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mr. Fajardo said a minor correction needs to be made to condition 8 and read it into the record.\par

After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the agenda item in question, indicate support, opposition, or neutrality on the agenda item, and then proceed to succinctly state the speaker’s position or present information.
If an attorney, or any other person appears before the Commission in a representative capacity, the attorney, or other representative shall also sign up in the Fort Lauderdale Police Department lobby. A member of the City Clerk’s Office Staff will be there to assist. After being recognized by the Mayor, the speaker should approach the podium, identify the client(s) being represented, and identify the agenda item in question. Pursuant to Section 3.13 of the Charter of the City of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the Mayor shall maintain order at all meetings, and the Police Department, upon instructions of the Mayor, shall expel any person from the meeting who refuses to obey the order of the Mayor in relation to preserving order at the meetings. In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s request, Mr. Francis discussed the way funds are managed. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s request, Linda Short, Finance Department Director, and Glen Marcos, Procurement Services Department Director, explained the factors considered by the Evaluation Committee (EC). Mr. Marcos said both MissionSquare and Nationwide had the opportunity to protest the EC\rquote s decision and did not exhaust that administrative remedy. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Commissioner Herbst said people should be able to choose the option that best suits them and asked if people can stay with their preferred provider. Mr. Marcos shared that the EC had that discussion and decided against it. He added that the committee relied heavily on Executive Summary reports from Burgess Chambers & Associates. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question, Mr. Marcos confirmed that the EC decided against a side-by-side comparison. Commissioner Herbst said the Commission is not bound by the decision of the EC. Mr. Marcos said the Commission\rquote s options include accepting, denying, or modifying the EC\rquote s recommendation.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Mr. Marcos and Ms. Short provided information on the members of the EC.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Greg Miller, designated representative of Corebridge Financial. Mr. Miller spoke in support of the EC\rquote s recommendation and said the industry standard is to go with only one provider. He said providers now offer more than one option so the need for multiple vendors is not necessary and can cause confusion. \par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\f0 Commissioner Glassman introduced this Resolution, which was read by title only.\cf1\f2\par

\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Connis Brown, 190 N Federal Highway, of Brown Robert LLC speaking on behalf of Dicey Riley's. \pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Adam Peterson, 421 N Andrews Avenue, General Counsel for The Restaurant People and Urban Street Development. \pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Robert Lochrie, 699 N Federal Highway, member of PACA, the Broward Foundation, and the Museum of Discovery and Science. \pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Carol Henderson, 10920 NW 3rd Street, representing the Board members of History Fort Lauderdale. Ms. Henderson expressed support for decertification of the special entertainment district.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Ellyn Bogdanoff, 1 E Broward Boulevard, representing Sway, Backyard, Fat Cats, and Munchies. \pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote comment about violent conduct in the area, Ms. Bogdanoff said increased enforcement has only been happening for one week. \pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Stephanie Toothaker, 901 Ponce De Leon Drive. Ms. Toothaker spoke in favor of decertification.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis recognized Robert Pignone, 110 S 3rd Avenue, Owner of Poorhouse. \pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Herbst\rquote s question, City Attorney McCartney said the 180-day time period is to allow businesses to transition to the requirements the Commission chooses to include in the Ordinance including receiving a waiver to convert to a restaurant in order to avoid noncompliance with the 300-foot obligation.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Mayor Trantalis\rquote question, Acting City Manager Cooper said decertification would cause the businesses to lose extended hours until 4:00 a.m., lose extended amplified sound levels, require a distance of 300-feet between establishments licensed to sell alcoholic beverages unless they are a restaurant or a hotel with a bar, and the restaurant must account for at least 50% of the proceeds. The 180-day time period is to allow establishments to come into compliance with the new rules.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Acting City Manager Cooper confirmed that the Second Reading of this Ordinance would take place at the November 17, 2026 meeting.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s question, Acting City Manager Cooper confirmed that if the Ordinance passes Second Reading on November 17, 2026, establishments would have to immediately comply with the 2:00 a.m. and 3:00 a.m. closing times and the new sound level requirements. \pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par

\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question, Acting City Manager Cooper said the cost for compliance depends on the path each establishment chooses. He added that the basic hourly rate is currently $140 and the special exemption process for the distance separation with the Board of Adjustment is approximately $1,400.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s concern of adding a financial hardship to the businesses, Mr. Fajardo said there is some flexibility in the rate and added that the Commission could set up a permit process specific to this district. Vice Mayor Sorensen requested that the City Manager, staff, stakeholders, and Mr. Fajardo work on figuring out a process for compliance with distance separation after this meeting.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Mr. Fajardo said a distance separation waiver can be requested through the Board of Adjustment for anywhere within the City. \pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Glassman\rquote s question, Mr. Fajardo said additional remedies or paths could be discussed with the City Attorney\rquote s Office and presented at the Second Reading.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 In response to Commissioner Beasley-Pittman\rquote s question, Acting City Manager Cooper said the number of businesses in the district was factored into the 180-day period along with necessary public notices.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 Mayor Trantalis, Commissioner Herbst, and Commissioner Glassman agreed that the 180-day period is a safe approach. Acting City Manager Cooper added that the lack of common control and the failure to maintain that for at least 180 days are the basis for this decertification.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\f0 At Vice Mayor Sorensen\rquote s request, Acting City Manager Cooper and City Attorney McCartney confirmed that, upon final passage on November 17, 2026, operating hours revert to 2:00 a.m. and 3:00 a.m. and sound levels return to the normal standard. The only thing that has an 180-day allowance relates to distance noncompliance.\par
\pard\nowidctlpar\li2520\f1\par
